findings.seen: The body text is visibly smaller than the header labels ('Return policy', 'Billing cycle'). It measures about 14px against the 16px of the header labels. The size comes from inheritance: Veneer sets `--bs-body-font-size: var(--vn-size-2)` (0.875rem) in src/styles/_tokens.scss, and src/styles/components/_accordion.scss declares no font size on `.accordion-body`.
findings.expected: In Bootstrap, `.accordion-body` (node_modules/bootstrap/scss/_accordion.scss) sets only padding and inherits the body type. Bootstrap's `--bs-body-font-size` is `$font-size-base` = 1rem, so the body text renders at 16px, the same size as `.accordion-button`, which sets `font-size($font-size-base)`. The size is a documented global token choice: guides/veneer.md's token table notes that `--bs-body-font-size` reads `--vn-size-2`. It is not an accordion partial defect. I refer it to the Orchestrator to confirm that the 14px body is an intended departure from Bootstrap.

findings.region: Top-left: the 'Shipment actions' toggle above the open menu. The same applies to the toggle in every open-menu frame in this slice: dropdown-menu, dropdown-menu-end ('Invoice actions'), dropdown-center ('Dock actions'), dropdown-menu-inverted ('Manifest actions'), dropdown-menu-hover, dropdown-menu-focus, and both toggles in every dropdown-align-* frame, in all four variants.
findings.seen: The menu is shown, but its toggle paints the resting btn-secondary fill. The fill matches the closed 'Carrier options' toggle in dropdown-closed--light-1280.png, so nothing on the button reads as opened. The specimen markup explains this: in app/browser/constants.ts, in DROPDOWN_SPECIMENS, around line 1937, the toggle carries aria-expanded="true" but not the `show` class, and only the menu carries `show`. The NAV_SPECIMENS tabs toggle in the same file does set `show` on its toggle. The stylesheet is not at fault: src/styles/components/_button.scss already ships the `.btn.show` rule.
findings.expected: In Bootstrap 5.3.8, the dropdown plugin adds `show` to both the toggle and the menu when a dropdown opens. node_modules/bootstrap/scss/_buttons.scss, in the `.btn` block (`.btn-check:checked + &, :not(.btn-check) + &:active, &:first-child:active, &.active, &.show`), then paints the toggle with `--bs-btn-active-color` and `--bs-btn-active-bg`. An open btn-secondary toggle therefore shows its darker active fill, not the resting fill. The fix belongs in the specimen markup: add `show` to the toggle in the open-menu specimens (the Dropdown menu family and the Dropdown align family).

findings.region: The whole 'Toggle' button (btn-primary, pressed). The same appears in toggle-pressed--dark-390.png.
findings.seen: In dark mode the pressed btn-primary is a light sky-blue with white text: it is lighter than a primary fill. In toggle-pressed--light-1280.png the pressed state is a darker blue. The pressed paint therefore changes direction between the modes. This comes from src/styles/components/_button.scss, where `--bs-btn-active-bg` is color-mix(--vn-state-mixer 22%, role base). src/styles/_tokens.scss sets `state-mixer` to white in the dark theme.
findings.expected: Bootstrap 5.3.8 generates `.btn-primary` through the button-variant mixin (node_modules/bootstrap/scss/_buttons.scss, `@each $color, $value in $theme-colors` with `@include button-variant`). Its active background is shade-color($primary, 20%), which is #0a58ca, and the mixin sets it the same way in both colour modes. A pressed primary toggle therefore paints a darker blue under data-bs-theme="dark" as well. The Veneer tint may be a deliberate theme decision. Refer it to the colour lens to decide whether it is an accepted deviation.

findings.seen: The two disabled items render in visibly different tones. 'Base archive' is a mid grey. 'Base export' is a much paler grey, lighter again in dark mode. The cause is in source: the elements-layer rule `button:disabled` in /home/user/veneer/src/styles/elements/_button.scss applies `opacity: var(--vn-button-opacity)` (0.65, from _tokens.scss). The component rule `.nav-link:disabled` in /home/user/veneer/src/styles/components/_nav.scss sets the colour but never resets opacity, so the button is also faded to 65%.
findings.expected: Bootstrap 5.3.8 gives both items the same colour, `var(--bs-nav-link-disabled-color)` = `--bs-secondary-color`. The rule is `.nav-link { &.disabled, &:disabled { color: ... } }` in bootstrap/scss/_nav.scss. Bootstrap's reboot sets no opacity on `button:disabled`, so the disabled button and the disabled anchor match. The fix is to have `.nav-link:disabled` reset `opacity: 1`, or to stop the elements-layer opacity from reaching a `.nav-link`.

Hover therefore lowers the link's contrast against the dark page. In the light siblings (nav-base-hover--light-*, nav-tabs-hover--light-*), hover darkens the link against a white page, which raises contrast, so only the dark variant loses legibility on hover. In /home/user/veneer/src/styles/_tokens.scss, the $dark map entry 'link-hover' (around line 93) is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--vn-link-base) 80%, black)`, with link-hover-rgb 63, 148, 190.
